dimension_justifications.soundness: The true-H oracle tower identity, its terminal k=N handling, the FIT-frozen conditioning argument, and the finite-family empirical-Bernstein/Bonferroni construction are sound under their stated count-exchangeable and task-i.i.d. assumptions. The packaged main replay also reproduces exactly from the derived count manifest. However, Lemma 1 as stated contains a false existence conclusion and its printed proof omits the even-N central-tie case; a separate model-motivation remark makes an unsupported inference from task demeaning. These are substantive, repairable technical defects.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The oracle/fitted-score boundary, CAL-versus-TEST status, terminal convention, and TV diagnostic scope are unusually explicit and easy to audit. The proof is readable, but its central-tie omission and the unqualified k*(alpha) statement make the formal presentation less reliable than it appears.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The narrow contribution is a clear, exact count-exchangeable replay analysis: a FIT-frozen plug-in stopping rule screened by held-out task-level replay loss. It is carefully distinguished from ordered online stopping and correctness/cost claims, but is a limited replay endpoint and its claimed supporting monotonicity result needs correction.

paper_summary: The paper models each task by a full-N binary pass count, treats an observed prefix as a uniform without-replacement replay, proves an oracle true-mixture posterior flip identity for eligible stopping times, and evaluates a distinct FIT-fitted posterior score. Conditional on FIT, it CAL-screens a pre-declared finite family using empirical-Bernstein UCBs with Bonferroni correction; TEST is presented as descriptive replay evidence only.
strongest_verified_contribution: For a fixed FIT-frozen fitted-score rule, the exact replay loss is a bounded function g(K) of an i.i.d. CAL task count. Therefore the conditional empirical-Bernstein bound and Bonferroni simultaneous selection argument genuinely bound marginal count-replay flip risk under the explicitly stated task-i.i.d. model; this does not rely on identifying the fitted score with the true-H posterior.
strengths: Theorem 1 correctly separates the true-H oracle posterior from the fitted score. Given a bounded prefix-filtration stopping time, the terminal state has x_N=K and zero flip, so the tower identity needs no union bound over stopping times.

Theorem 2 conditions on FIT before treating g_r(K_i) as bounded i.i.d. CAL observations. The reported 60 fixed-budget-by-level entries plus four BAYES-H levels are a conservative J=64 finite family, and the supplied standard-library replay reproduces the main JSON byte-for-byte from the declared count manifest.

The frozen-rule TV objective is correctly posed as a capacity-constrained linear program. Independent small-state enumeration agrees with the stated two-sided greedy solution; the paper appropriately labels the resulting curves as assumed-ball sensitivities rather than population-shift certificates.
The manuscript is forthright that its quantities are binary pass-count replay flip and expected replay count, not ordered deployment, delivered-answer correctness, or realized cost.
questions: Will the authors repair Lemma 1 by proving the K=N/2 case separately and by conditioning k*(alpha) on existence on the odd grid (or adding an explicit full-N fallback)?

What estimand and finite-group correction, if any, support the claim that the task-demeaned correlation diagnoses absence of latent within-task dependence? If none, will the authors remove that inference and retain only the identifiable count-mixture statement?
Will Proposition 1 define tau*(alpha) only when V(0)<=alpha, or explicitly specify the convention for an empty feasible-radius set?

issues.location: Lemma 1, manuscript PDF p.4 / source/paper.tex:259-275; Appendix A 'The reflection identity', PDF p.10 / source/appendix_proofs.tex:32-48.
issues.observed_evidence: For even N and K=N/2, the paper defines the full vote as negative. For any odd k, hypergeometric symmetry gives U_{N/2}(k)=P(x_k>k/2)=1/2. But the displayed reflection equates it with R_{N-K}(k)=R_{N/2}(k), which is 0 by the paper's own indicator 1{K>N/2}. Thus the reflection step does not cover the central-tie count. Moreover, for N=32, H=delta_16, and alpha=0.05, f_16(k)=1/2 at every odd k in {1,...,31}; hence the displayed minimum defining k*(alpha) is over an empty set, contrary to 'well defined for every mixture H'. The supplied audit checks only K>N/2 reversal cases, so it does not repair either logical point.
issues.why_it_matters: The monotonicity inequality itself is readily repairable, but the lemma currently combines an incomplete proof with a false universal feasibility conclusion. It is presented as the justification for binary-searchable fixed-budget certification, so the formal statement should not be accepted as written.
issues.required_fix: Handle K=N/2 separately using hypergeometric symmetry (f_{N/2}(k)=1/2 for odd k), restrict the reflection argument to K<N/2, and replace the unconditional k*(alpha) claim with 'when the odd-grid feasible set is nonempty' or include an explicit N-budget fallback and state its convention. Extend the exact audit to the center case and the no-feasible-budget behavior.
issues.verification_test: For every even N in the audit range, assert f_{N/2}(k)=1/2 for all odd k; then test H=delta_{N/2}, alpha<1/2 and confirm the revised definition returns the documented no-feasible/fallback outcome rather than an undefined minimum.
issues.evidence_needed: No new experiment is needed; a corrected proof and exact finite-state audit suffice.

issues.location: Remark 1 'Why the mixture, not the correlation', manuscript PDF p.3 / source/paper.tex:231-244, especially the inference from rho_FE approximately -1/(N-1) to 'essentially all observed correlation is across-task heterogeneity'.
issues.observed_evidence: Within every task with n rollouts, residuals y_ij-ybar_i sum to zero. Consequently the average off-diagonal residual covariance is mechanically -1/(n-1) times the average diagonal residual variance; its corresponding correlation floor -1/(n-1) occurs regardless of the original latent within-task dependence. A task-demeaned correlation therefore cannot establish that latent within-task dependence is absent or that 'essentially all' observed dependence is cross-task. This also conflicts with the paper's later, correct statement that count-only data cannot identify whether within-task correlation is dominant.
issues.why_it_matters: The remark is used to motivate replacing correlation-based reasoning by the mixture view. The replay framework need not make this causal-decomposition claim, but the stated inference is not identified by the described statistic and overstates what the carrier demonstrates.
issues.required_fix: Remove the conclusion about the source of correlation, or provide a precisely defined estimand and an analysis that remains informative after the finite-group demeaning constraint. Retain the defensible claim that the replay flip functional is determined by the count mixture under the specified replay model.
issues.verification_test: Show algebraically that the proposed statistic is not fixed by the within-task zero-sum identity, or else delete the latent-dependence conclusion and check that all remaining correlation wording agrees with the stated count-only limitation.
issues.evidence_needed: Either an identified, correctly finite-sample-adjusted within-task dependence analysis with its raw observations, or a claim narrowing; no new ordered-online experiment is required merely to remove the inference.

issues.observed_evidence: The proposition defines tau*(alpha)=max{R:V(R)<=alpha} without a feasibility qualification. If alpha<V(0)=sum_K Hhat[K]g(K), this set is empty and has no maximum. The supplied implementation returns 0.0 in this case even though R=0 does not satisfy the displayed inequality. The named reported levels appear feasible, but the proposition is stated generally.
issues.why_it_matters: This is a formal edge-case error in an otherwise correct LP sensitivity result. It can mislabel an infeasible rule as having a zero critical radius.
issues.required_fix: State the definition only for V(0)<=alpha, or define an explicit infeasible sentinel/convention distinct from a feasible radius of zero; align the implementation and any figure/table reporting with that convention.
issues.verification_test: Use any frozen g,Hhat pair with alpha<V(0) and verify that the revised code reports infeasible/undefined rather than a radius claimed to satisfy V(R)<=alpha.
issues.evidence_needed: No new data; a definition and implementation edge-case test suffice.

ethics_concerns: No distinct ethics violation is established within the frozen replay-scope submission. The paper appropriately discloses that the supplied analysis does not measure deployed correctness, latency, tokens, or cancellation behavior.
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was produced by an isolated AI subagent for internal pre-submission quality control, using only the specified frozen Round-4 submission snapshot.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A corrected complete Lemma 1 proof and audit covering K=N/2 plus explicit no-feasible-budget/fallback semantics.
Removal or valid identification of the task-demeaned correlation inference, with wording consistent with the count-only limitation.
An explicit infeasible-radius convention for Proposition 1 and a passing edge-case test.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: A counterexample to the oracle tower identity under the stated true-H count-exchangeable replay model or evidence that the implementation uses a different terminal/stopping rule.
A mismatch between the frozen count manifest, the FIT/CAL rule selection, and the reported main replay JSON.
Evidence that the claimed CAL family was not FIT-frozen or that its empirical-Bernstein/Bonferroni coverage calculation differs from the implemented one.
review_limitations: Per isolation instructions, this review used only the frozen Round-4 snapshot and did not inspect raw parquet data, prior review rounds, author working directories, or other reviewer reports.
The main OMR numerical replay was independently rerun only conditional on the supplied derived count manifest; secondary recovered runners were inspected as provenance, not rerun end-to-end.
Literature positioning was assessed from the snapshot's scoped primary-source records rather than an unrestricted external survey.
